_schema: Shared conformance fixture for trust-policy glob matching, consumed by
BOTH the C++ mirror (core/tests/trust_policy_test.cpp -> TrustPolicyStore
::evaluate/globMatch) and the Python source of truth
(computer-use/computer_use_mcp/policy.py, fnmatch-based -- see its test
at computer-use/tests/test_policy.py). Keep this filename/path and the
vector object shape stable across both consumers.
Each vector in "vectors" is a single glob-match probe:
pattern  - the glob rule pattern under test.
value    - the string matched against `pattern`.
tool     - true => probe TOOL-field matching semantics
(case-SENSITIVE, e.g. TrustPolicyStore::evaluate()'s tool arg).
app      - true => probe APP-field matching semantics
(case-INSENSITIVE, '*'/'?' cross path separators like
fnmatch, e.g. TrustPolicyStore::evaluate()'s app arg).
Exactly one of tool/app is true per vector.
expected - whether `pattern` should match `value` under that context.
Seeded with the proven-divergent cases between Qt's
QRegularExpression::wildcardToRegularExpression() and Python's
fnmatch.translate(): (1) '*' must cross path separators ('/' and '\\'),
and (2) a leading '^' inside a bracket expression ('[^bank]') is a
LITERAL caret in fnmatch -- only a leading '!' negates -- whereas plain
regex bracket syntax treats '^' as negation.

vectors.note: app glob must match across a path separator (NonPathWildcardConversion)
regression guard: no-separator case must keep matching
leading '^' in [...] is LITERAL (fnmatch), not negation: 'x' is not one of ^,b,a,n,k
leading '^' in [...] is LITERAL (fnmatch): 'b' IS one of ^,b,a,n,k
regression guard: '!' still negates -- 'x' is not b,a,n,k so it matches
regression guard: '!' still negates -- 'b' IS excluded
regression guard: plain prefix-star tool match
regression guard: tool matching stays case-SENSITIVE
regression guard: app matching stays case-INSENSITIVE
